detail.note: looksRss = Ruby's measured default-disabled answer (body EXACTLY 'RSS feeds disabled', length 18, content-type EXACTLY text/html; charset=utf-8 - receipts C:/localProjects/brandonDojoTech/tmp/act172-175-evidence/ruby-reference-act172-act175.json and .../ruby-reference-missing-mark.json, oracle booted from reference-harness/browser/engines/ruby.json on synthetic-v1) OR a real enabled feed (XML declaration / <rss> / <rdf:RDF>, or an application/rss+xml|atom+xml|xml content-type). Both .rss arms here take the first branch, because Ruby itself answers exactly that with rss_enabled FALSE (mod/format/lib/card/mod/format.rb:3). The grade is pinned to the measured bytes: matchesRubyDisabledAnswer must be true on BOTH arms, and the same mark's .json arm must still answer application/json and NOT look like an RSS answer (the positive control). No enabled-feed acceptance is claimed - nothing here observes a real feed document. What this leg DOES now establish: the (.:format) route arms are served with Ruby's bytes rather than resolved as a card name (a5bc4702; vm-staging-server.mjs:3139/:3171/:3216), which is why rssShape.slotIds is now empty - the format arm answers no card page.
